today.question_title: Maximize the Distance Between Points on a Square
hints_cache: This problem follows the 'maximize the minimum' pattern, which is a classic signal to use Binary Search on the Answer. Instead of calculating the distance directly, try picking a target distance and checking if it's achievable.

To make the points easier to process, transform each 2D coordinate into a 1D value representing its distance along the perimeter (from $0$ to $4 \times side$). Sorting these values allows you to treat the square boundary like a sorted array.

For a fixed target distance $D$, you can use a greedy approach: pick a starting point, then skip forward until you find the first point that is at least $D$ Manhattan units away. Repeat this until you have picked $k$ points.

Be careful with the distance formula! While sorting by perimeter helps you pick points in order, the problem specifically asks for Manhattan distance: $|x_1 - x_2| + |y_1 - y_2|$. Use this formula when checking if two points are far enough apart.

The 'wrap-around' means your $k$-th point must also be at least $D$ away from your $1$-st point. Since $k$ is small, you can try starting your greedy selection from each of the first few points to see if any valid cycle exists.
